bullets.title: S&P 500 +1.8%, VIX at 16.31 as risk-on rally broadens
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures opened +1.25% to 7,528 and extended gains to +1.8% (7,563) intraday with VIX at 16.31. Memory/storage chipmakers led: MU +7.9%, WDC +15%, STX +7.9%, SNDK +3.2%—all at 52-week highs. Finance sector dominated breadth with 137 new highs; Electronic Technology added 33.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz reopening: oil -5%, inflation tail risk fades, Fed stays on hold
bullets.body: A US-Iran interim peace deal triggered WTI -5% and a broad -3-5% selloff in energy equities. 22V and Piper Sandler both frame lower oil as a consumer tailwind and disinflationary impulse that supports the Fed remaining on hold. Hedgeye's May CPI Nowcast is now tracking inside 4%, with one quarter-point hike repriced off the table—December hike probability ~71-72% vs. two hikes priced two days ago.

bullets.title: AI mid-cycle rotation underway: hyperscalers → infrastructure materials, small-cap semis
bullets.body: Multiple strategists flag AI transitioning from early-cycle buildout to a stockpicker's mid-cycle phase. Tight correlations are breaking as leadership rotates: compute → power → cooling → optical → memory → packaging. 22V notes QQQ upside calls trade at 60%+ premium to SPY, recommending a rotation into SPY or IWM. Small caps are outperforming Mag7; MAG7 stocks are down 7-10% YTD vs. SPX +30bps.

bullets.title: HDD super-cycle extends to CY28: MS raises WDC to $650, STX to $1,035
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Erik Woodring raises WDC and STX price targets after Asia supply checks show nearline HDD pricing shortages through CY28; current pricing <$15/TB with vendors targeting $25-30/TB over 2-3 years. Base-case FY28 EPS is 70% above consensus; bull case would 10x EPS from CY25-CY28. Hyperscalers are signing LTAs through 2032 and prioritizing storage over compute.

bullets.title: Anthropic Fable 5/Mythos 5 access banned by US export control; raises AI regulatory risk
bullets.body: The Trump administration directed Anthropic to disable global access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models citing national security; AWS reportedly flagged a jailbreak vulnerability to officials. This adds a new regulatory overhang to the AI trade at a time of slowing model-pricing growth and token-efficiency pressure, with 22V flagging it as a rotation catalyst away from hyperscalers.

bullets.title: US May industrial production soft (+0.1% vs +0.3% est) but breadth at cycle highs
bullets.body: May IP rose 0.1% m/m, below the 0.3% consensus, after April's 0.9% surge. Manufacturing gained 0.2% to its highest since late 2022, with AI-linked semiconductors and computers notable contributors. IP breadth improved to a 12-month high; Empire Fed PMI retreated 13.9 pts to +5.7 headline but the ISM-adjusted version held at 53.4. Piper Sandler sees activity remaining solid through H1 2027, aided by lagged Fed easings and tech buildout.

bullets.title: Fox acquires Roku for $22B ($160/sh); FOXA -14% on dilution, Roku near flat
bullets.body: Fox agreed to acquire Roku for $160/share ($96 cash + 0.9693 Class A shares) in a ~$22B EV deal, funded with $12B in bridge financing. The combined company becomes the third-largest US TV player by viewership (~10% share vs. YouTube 13%), with ~$5B EBITDA growing ~8% CAGR and $400M run-rate cost synergies. FOXA fell -14-17% on equity dilution and leverage concerns (pro-forma net leverage 2.9x); Citi calls it an overreaction and maintains Buy at $78 PT.

bullets.title: NAHB Housing Index slips to 35; 35% of builders now cutting prices
bullets.body: June NAHB Housing Market Index fell 2 points to 35, missing the unchanged consensus. Price cuts rose to 35% of builders (from 32% in May), though the average reduction held at 6%. Current conditions eased from 40 to 38; regional breadth was mixed with the South declining. PSC Macro forecasts a U-shaped housing recovery.

bullets.title: JPM: US headline CPI expected at 3.9% through July; core stable at 2.8-2.9%
bullets.body: JPMorgan's monthly inflation forecast update pegs US headline CPI at 3.9% YoY through July 2026, with PCE also at 3.9% and core CPI stable at 2.8-2.9%. Hedgeye's Nowcast sees May CPI as cycle peak; June is tracking inside 4%, consistent with one fewer Fed hike being priced.

bullets.title: AI leadership rotating within semis: INTC foundry, MRVL custom silicon, ALAB interconnect
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's semis bus tour finds AI infrastructure value shifting toward interconnect, scale-up, optics, packaging, and memory rather than raw compute. INTC's 14A process targets 0.5 defect density with risk production in 2028; MRVL's custom silicon opportunity is $4B-$10B with connectivity growing ~70%; ALAB content per XPU is already ~$1,000 and rising. TSEM's silicon photonics demand is accelerating with management likely to raise FY26 revenue targets above $2.8B.

bullets.title: META token-limiting AI spend internally; MSFT CEO argues value accrues to enterprise, not frontier models
bullets.body: META is tracking billions in internal AI spending in 2026 and is implementing token limits plus an AI Gateway dashboard in 2027 to control costs. Microsoft's CEO blogged that AI value should accrue via enterprise learning loops and sovereign company-specific systems rather than frontier model concentration—a thesis that suggests competitive moats are shifting toward application layer incumbents.

bullets.title: Regional banks (KRE) seeing positive technical breakout with bullish fundamental alignment
bullets.body: Two independent research analysts (Roque and Hebel) are converging on a bullish regional bank thesis, with KRE/KRX exhibiting a base/breakout technical setup alongside improving fundamentals. Separately, JPM's financials note flags a macro tailwind for consumer finance from the Middle East deal and crude direction, while COF May credit data showed DQs improved 11bps m/m and NCOs improved 12bps m/m.

bullets.title: Juneteenth holiday (June 19) to compress FX volumes 35-50%; recovery within one day
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs analysis of 2021-2025 Juneteenth data shows most major FX pairs trade at 0.46x-0.76x of normal 30-day average daily volume on the holiday, with USDTRY, USDMXN, and EURPLN seeing the heaviest compression (0.46x-0.61x). Asia NDF crosses and EM deliverables are less affected. Volumes typically recover to near-normal within one trading day.

bullets.title: Colombia right-wing candidate leads 51-53% ahead of June 21 runoff; energy sector primary beneficiary
bullets.body: JPMorgan flags de la Espriella holding a 4-8 point polling lead over Cepeda heading into the June 21 runoff. A right-wing win would likely accelerate US security cooperation, put Colombia on track for an IMF Precautionary Liquidity Line, and create the clearest structural change potential in the energy sector; a Cepeda win maintains Petro-era policies and delays IMF stabilization.

bullets.title: Shanghai freight index +43% YoY—accelerating gross margin headwind for retailers
bullets.body: Hedgeye's freight tracker shows the Shanghai freight index up 43% YoY, accelerating from +22% the prior week, representing a meaningful gross margin headwind for consumer goods retailers heading into 2H reporting.

bullets.title: FOMC on June 17 coincides with GS equity flows webinar; macro volatility re-emerging after spring rally
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs notes US equities are consolidating after a strong spring rally with macro volatility re-emerging. The FOMC press conference on June 17 follows a string of strong macroeconomic data prints. GS is hosting its monthly equity flow and positioning webinar the same day, covering YTD flows and mega-IPO implications.

bullets.title: Online ad stocks underperformed S&P since ME conflict; Cannes as potential re-rating catalyst
bullets.body: BofA notes the internet subsector equal-weighted average (>$5B cap) is up only 1% since the Middle East conflict started on 2/27 vs. S&P +8%, with online travel most impacted (2-3pt room-night pressure in Q1/Q2). Citi's top ad picks into Cannes '26 are GOOGL, AMZN, META, RDDT, and APP, with AI-driven agentic commerce monetization expected as the core theme.

bullets.title: European equities face stagnating macro; UBS sees Stoxx 600 above year-end target with downside risks building
bullets.body: UBS flags Europe entering a challenging phase with GDP growth 2026-27 below 2025 levels and 2026 consensus EPS growth of 16% looking unlikely given surging input costs. The OECD CLI has rolled into a slowdown regime; earnings are increasingly concentrated in financials and energy. UBS favors defensives, utilities, telecoms, pharma, and AI enablers with pricing power while cautioning on consumer cyclicals.
